judgment.rationale: Both are Indicators at the same BASIC 4 rank under Content Standard B4.1.1.3 ('factors, multiples and squared numbers'), so the direction rests on statement content, not code order or shared parentage. The second SFI (B4.1.1.3.1) asks learners to determine the set of factors of a given number up to 50; the first (B4.1.1.3.2) asks learners to determine the highest common factor of any two whole numbers between 1 and 50. Generating a complete factor set for a single number is the enabling skill that is then extended to two numbers and to comparing/selecting the greatest shared factor, a substantive increase in complexity within the same 1-50 number range (LC tags 'factors'/'numbers' vs 'factors'/'hcf'). Proficiency with factor sets therefore supports success with HCF, giving buildsTowards from the second endpoint to the first.

B5.1.1.1 concerns quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals (up to 100,000/1,000,000), while B5.1.1.3 concerns factors, multiples, composite, even, odd and prime numbers from 1 to 100. Same-rank developmental direction therefore lacks substantive support, so a symmetric relatesTo is the appropriate judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/continuation audit context and truncated source evidence, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 (rank 2) Indicators in Strand 2: Algebra, so same-grain comparison is appropriate. B6.2.1.1.8 (Sub-Strand 1: Pattern and Relationships) asks learners to describe a table/chart relationship using a mathematical expression, while B6.2.2.1.1 (Sub-Strand 2: Algebraic Expressions) asks learners to demonstrate understanding of algebraic expressions as phrases with letters and operators. These are substantively coherent: symbolic-expression understanding and expressing a tabular relationship symbolically reinforce each other. However, the evidence does not establish a directional dependency at equal rank: the pattern indicator is sequenced in the earlier sub-strand while the conceptual expression indicator could equally be viewed as foundational, and the lexical nomination signals (single shared token 'mathematical', weak code/page proximity) add no directional support. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards (same statement grain, same resolved Grade coordinate rank 2) but sit in different strands: B6.4.2.2 (Strand 4: Data / Sub-Strand 2: Chance or Probability) concerns identifying all possible outcomes and determining theoretical and experimental probability, while B6.1.3.1 (Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 3: Fractions) concerns strategies for comparing and operating on common, decimal and percent fractions. There is genuine conceptual coherence, since probabilities of outcomes are quantified and compared as common fractions, decimals or percents, so the fraction work meaningfully reinforces the probability work. However, the supplied statement texts contain no explicit linkage (the probability standard never names fractions, decimals or percents), the nomination evidence is only shared Grade ancestry, weak same-rank proximity, a weak 'b6' code prefix and generic stem overlap ('demonstrate an understanding of'), and both endpoints have truncated source evidence with omitted items. That is insufficient to assert a same-rank developmental direction, so a symmetric relation is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 1) under the same Content Standard B5.1.1.1 ('Demonstrate an understanding of quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1,000,000') within Strand 1 Number, Sub-strand 1 Counting, Representation & Cardinality. B5.1.1.1.6 asks learners to skip count forwards/backwards in 500s and 1000s up to and from 100,000, while B5.1.1.1.1 asks learners to model number quantities up to 1,000,000 with graph sheets and multi-base blocks; the LCs for both carry the shared 'place value' tag and large-number ranges. This is substantive complementary coherence — concrete modelling of large quantities and structured counting by place-value-sized intervals reinforce the same place-value understanding — but at equal grade rank the evidence does not substantiate that proficiency in one is developmentally needed to succeed at the other (indicator numbering .1 vs .6 is source order, not semantic sequence), so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Evidence limitations: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and the shared parent Content Standard carries a merge decision arising from a stale 'CONT'D' duplicate, so ancestor text is used only as coarse topical context.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 4 Content Standard B4.2.2.2 ("Solve one-step equations involving a symbol to represent an unknown number") in Strand 2: Algebra, Sub-strand 2: Unknowns, Expressions and Equations, and both are at coordinate rank 0 (BASIC 4), so direction rests on statement content rather than grade. B4.2.2.2.2 asks learners to describe orally the meaning of a given one-step equation with one unknown (LC tags: meaning, one-step equation, oral description, unknown), i.e. interpreting what the equation asserts about the unknown. B4.2.2.2.4 asks learners to solve a given one-step equation using "guess and check" (LC tags: equations, guess and check, one-step), which requires substituting trial values and judging whether the equation is satisfied — an operation that depends on understanding the equation's meaning. Proficiency in interpreting the equation therefore supports success in the trial-and-verify solution strategy, supporting second_to_first; the reverse (solving procedurally supporting oral interpretation) is less directly supported by the texts. Shared wording alone ("given", "one-step", "equation") was not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the interpret-then-solve content distinction. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so bounded exemplar detail may qualify this reading.

Proficiency with such division therefore supports success in solving the one-step equations, giving a same-grade second-to-first developmental direction rather than mere topical overlap (the only lexical overlap, 'number', is not itself probative). judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (same grade rank 2) in Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 1: Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality, but under different Content Standards: B6.1.1.1.2 asks learners to read and write numbers in figures and in words up to 1,000,000,000 (LCs: read/write numbers in figures and words), while B6.1.1.2.2 asks learners to count and convert Hindu Arabic numbers to Roman numerals up to 100 (C) and vice versa (LCs: count Hindu Arabic numbers to 100, convert both directions). They cohere as complementary work on representing and naming numbers in alternative notations, so substantive conceptual coherence exists. However, neither is developmentally required for the other: billion-scale place-value reading/writing far exceeds the 100 ceiling of the Roman numeral work, and Roman numeral conversion adds a distinct symbol system rather than deepening figure-and-word notation. Token/code/hierarchy overlap is weak ('numbers', 'up to', shared b6.1.1 prefix) and same-rank direction lacks substantive support, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.
